dedupe_keys.name: north american urban tree spatial dataset 30 cities 3 9 million trees

description: This dataset standardises the public tree inventories of 30 cities in the United States and Canada into one spatial table of urban trees with species and trunk size. Leona Neftaliem compiled it in 2023 with cleaning code for each city and presented it as a poster at AGU 2023. There are two versions: 4.7 million trees combining all inventories whatever their year, and 3.9 million trees likely still alive in 2023, each with country, state, city, inventory year, coordinates in EPSG:4326, botanical and common species names and diameter at breast height in centimetres. Coverage includes Atlanta, Austin, Baltimore, Boston, Calgary, Columbus, Edmonton and other cities. Format and access: CSV files in a public repository, as a combined set and by city, with species code tables. Licence: MIT for the repository, while each city's source terms (PDDL, CC0, open government licences) still apply. Caveats: inventories date from different years and mostly cover public street and park trees. It supports urban heat, carbon and storm-damage exposure studies at continental scale. Related catalogue records are the NYC 2015 Street Tree Census and Copenhagen's street tree data, examples of the city inventories such sets combine.
